<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **18** documentable anchor(s).

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via helpText (literal, a string literal in appTranslationDataShape))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via helpText (literal, a string literal in appTranslationDataShape))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx`  _(via helpText (literal, a string literal in appTranslationDataShape), metadataForms (literal, a string literal in walkFormField))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx`  _(via helpText (literal, a string literal in appTranslationDataShape))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectui/layout-dsl.mdx`  _(via helpText (literal, a string literal in appTranslationDataShape))_
- `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx`  _(via helpText (literal, a string literal in appTranslationDataShape), metadataForms (literal, a string literal in walkFormField))_
- `content/docs/ui/views.mdx`  _(via helpText (literal, a string literal in appTranslationDataShape))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via helpText (literal, a string literal in appTranslationDataShape))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via helpText (literal, a string literal in appTranslationDataShape))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via helpText (literal, a string literal in appTranslationDataShape), metadataForms (literal, a string literal in walkFormField))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via helpText (literal, a string literal in appTranslationDataShape))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0f6a1e518f3c4639b03f86a8c07d9d08d91bddb6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4e7ceb6eb638056c54a36314956642ae2a3065f3` — the merge of head `fa2b9fc7dfa26ab486be4a9a604b5d6922da414a` into base `0f6a1e518f3c4639b03f86a8c07d9d08d91bddb6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4e7ceb6eb638056c54a36314956642ae2a3065f3 && git checkout 4e7ceb6eb638056c54a36314956642ae2a3065f3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0f6a1e518f3c4639b03f86a8c07d9d08d91bddb6 fa2b9fc7dfa26ab486be4a9a604b5d6922da414a && git checkout -B drift-repro 0f6a1e518f3c4639b03f86a8c07d9d08d91bddb6 && git merge --no-ff fa2b9fc7dfa26ab486be4a9a604b5d6922da414a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0f6a1e518f3c4639b03f86a8c07d9d08d91bddb6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0f6a1e518f3c4639b03f86a8c07d9d08d91bddb6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The seat judges this a flake, for three reasons:
- The case spawns a child process synchronously, and the whole file took 67 s on the runner against the 5 s default case timeout.
- This PR touches no `packages/cli` file and nothing the start or deployment check reads; its scope is `metadataForms` translation slots, the resolver and the lint extractor.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8f1f70ffa5c34c3c708669cbf2ccf73ddbfdf324`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts, packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts + packages/lint/src/i18n-walk.ts

Read: card #36950 (body and both comments), this PR's body, file list and net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on the head. The eleven `*.metadata-forms.generated.ts` packs are generated output and were not reviewed; they were read only to check that the schema, the resolver and the extractor agree with what they hold. Placeholders below are written `TYPE`, `PATH`, `VALUE`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set, widened: right.** A `metadataForms.TYPE.fields.PATH` entry now accepts `options`, a record from string to string (`translation.zod.ts:2551`), on all three faces built from `appTranslationDataShape` (`TranslationData`, `TranslationItem`, `PlatformTranslationData`). Before this head the strict entry refused the key. It is the leaf shape the five sibling option maps already use (object field, action param, picklist, dashboard global filter, flow screen field). Nothing is narrowed.
- **Refusal text, changed: right.** `choices` and `values` on that entry are refused before and after. The two new `aliases` rows only name the rename in the unknown-key message, and both alias-integrity halves hold: neither spelling is in the shape, and `options` is.
- **Served surface: right.** `resolveMetadataFormLabels` now overlays `options[].label` for the request locale on every field row that has a path, nested rows by dot path. An option's `value`, its position and its other keys pass through; a missing or empty translation keeps the authored label. Its server caller is `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts:3691`. No export is added or removed and no signature moves.
- **Extractor surface: right.** `collectExpectedEntries` gains 185 registry-driven entries with a six-segment path and source `metadataFormField`. The list-column pass filters on `path[4] === 'label'` (`i18n-walk.ts:2769`) and is unaffected, and `dedupeByPath` collapses the two `deleteBehavior` variants of one path. No application's coverage number moves by default: the CLI counts the `metadataForms` baseline only for a stack that ships the group or passes `--include-platform`.
- **Packs agree.** Each of the eleven packs holds 37 `options` blocks and 185 leaves under nine forms, nested at `fields[PATH].options[VALUE]`, which is the address the schema declares, the resolver reads and the extractor emits. That matches the PR's reading: 38 rows, 37 distinct paths, 185 distinct keys.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right, and `Metadata-protocol: added` is right: one new key an author can write, nothing removed or tightened. Both lines are in the PR body and in the changeset body.
- `@objectstack/spec` at `minor` satisfies the kind. `@objectstack/lint` and `@objectstack/platform-objects` at `patch` are non-protocol moves. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.
- The changeset's bullets on served forms, extraction and shipped locales match the tree. Its sentence on the two alias spellings does not: that is finding S1 under ④.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag, the `choices` / `values` pair mirrors the object-field face:** answered. Right as rename pointers, which is all the object-field face has too. The changeset words them differently; see S1.
- **Dev flag, a non-string option value is passed through and not stringified:** answered, right on this face. `FormSelectOptionSchema` reuses `SelectOptionSchema.value`, a `SystemIdentifierSchema` string, so a parsed form has no other value type. The resolver and the extractor carry the same guard. The sibling faces that stringify declare `string | number | boolean`, which this face does not.
- **Dev flag, `check:i18n-coverage` could not be measured locally:** answered by CI. `Lint & Repo Gates` is green on the head.
- **`Skills-docs: none`:** holds for `skills/**`. On `main` the only mention is `skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md:180`, the group name in a list with no leaf under it. The group is the platform's by the CLI's own ownership rule (`stackAuthorsMetadataForms` in `packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-coverage.ts`): a stack that ships none of it is not asked for it. The docs half is N2.
- **`open_questions`:** none on the card or the PR.
- **SQL push-down:** nothing to judge. The change overlays an in-memory form; it adds no query, no id materialisation and no join.
- **Check-runs, newest run per name, read 2026-11-26T14:54Z:** every one is `success` or `skipped`, none failed. `Test Core (5/10)` failed once and its re-run succeeded; the aggregate `Test Core` is green. `Lint UI` reads `skipped` on both attempts of the run.
- **Landing class:** 3,873 changed lines, over 3,000, so the PR lands on an authorized APPROVED review. None is on the PR at read time. This record does not lift that.
- **Author:** `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no off-relay author note.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix. One should-fix, owing a delta review.

**S1 (should-fix) — the changeset says `choices` and `values` are accepted; the schema refuses both.**
`.changeset/36950-metadata-form-option-labels.md:12` reads "`choices` and `values` are accepted as its aliases, as on the object-field face." On the tree an `aliases` row of a `strictObject` is the rename pointer of the unknown-key refusal and never an accepted spelling (`packages/spec/src/shared/strict-object.ts`, the `aliases` option; `packages/spec/src/shared/suggestions.zod.ts:339-372`). A bundle that writes `choices` on this entry fails the parse with "Did you mean `choices` → `options`?", as it does on the object-field face; `translation.test.ts:1490` pins the same refusal on a sibling face. The schema is right and the sentence is not. It ships as CHANGELOG text that an upgrading author greps, and it reads as the lenient alias Prime Directive 12 forbids. The fix is on the prose face: say the two spellings are refused with a pointer to `options`. The PR body's "Spec, translation slot" bullet carries the same wording.

**`packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts`: holds.** Judged against the card (a slot for option names in the same bundle as the field labels around them) and against its first consumer, `translateFormField`.
- The key is the option `value`, which on a form field is always a system-identifier string, so a record key spells every value and a dot can never split one.
- A field whose own path is `options` (the field form's repeater, the object form's `fields.options`) does not collide with the new key: the path is a key of the `fields` record, and the option map sits one level below it.
- The jsdoc's claims hold against the resolver: it overlays the label of the entry whose value matches, it is keyed by value, and a value the row does not offer is never shown, because the resolver maps over the row's own options and never reads the map's other keys. N3 covers one phrase.

**`packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts`: holds.** What I tried to break:
- Two rows on one path with different option sets (`deleteBehavior`, `packages/spec/src/data/object.form.ts:371-382`): the shared values carry identical English names and one key each, and both rows translate.
- Nested rows: the console's repeater and composite take `fieldSpec.fields` when the form declares them (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/SchemaForm.tsx:2301-2304`), and its select draws `opt.label` and keys on `opt.value` (`SchemaForm.tsx:2458-2475`). So the overlay reaches a nested select and changes the words, never the stored value.
- An empty skeleton leaf falls through the locale chain. A non-string leaf, or a prototype key such as `constructor`, fails the string test and the authored label stays.
- The input is not mutated, an option's other keys (`color`, `visibleWhen`) are kept, a synthesized child has no options and is untouched, and a type with no bundle entry still returns the form by identity.
- The console's own caller (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/metadata-form-i18n.ts:171`) hands a bundle with no `options`, so its output is unchanged by this head.

**`packages/lint/src/i18n-walk.ts` (implementing): agrees with the contract.** Same path rule as the resolver (`field.field`, dot-joined, gated on a non-empty path), same guard (an object entry with a string value), key segments ending `PATH`, `options`, `VALUE`, and the seed is the authored English label. `FormSelectOptionSchema.label` is a required string, so `pushEntry` always emits. `check:i18n`, inside the green `Lint & Repo Gates`, is the gate that holds the committed packs equal to this walk.

Nits:
- N1 (nit, comment in a reviewed file): `i18n-resolver.ts:6078` still names the FormView route as `FormFieldSpec.label` / `helpText` / `placeholder`, and `:6088` says only those stay on it. `options[].label` rides the same route now. Accepted deviation: a fix moves a reviewed file, so it goes with the next touch.
- N2 (nit, prose face): `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx:575` and `:586-587` list label, helpText and placeholder as what `resolveMetadataFormLabels` overlays, and name no option names. This hand-written page is the one that teaches the group's leaves, and the `Skills-docs: none` reason speaks to `skills/**` only. Fix it there or in a follow-up card.
- N3 (nit, jsdoc in a reviewed file): `translation.zod.ts:2496`, "so a choice is named the same wherever the row is rendered", is true of the served form. The console's curated panels do not read this slot (note 1 below). Accepted deviation.

Out-of-diff notes (read, not reviewed):
1. The console's curated inspectors for report, dashboard, page and view render the bundled spec form through `localizeMetadataForm` over `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/metadata-form-zh-cn.ts`, which carries no `options`. The served form reaches the console through `ResourceEditPage` and `StudioBundleItemEditor`. So for three of the nine forms in the PR's reading the new slot does not reach the curated panel. `default-period-labels.ts` renames Default Period there for zh only, and its header still says the overlay "has no slot for option names". Whether the page and report selects in those panels read English in zh-CN was not run, since this review is read-only. It is a reading for the seat, and a card if it reproduces.
2. `form-option-labels.test.ts` is in the remainder, the lane seat's ACCEPT. It refuses any option name byte-equal to its English label in all ten locales, with no decision ledger of the kind `report-form-echo-decisions.test.ts` keeps. The packs reword loanwords to pass it, for example de `Textfeld` and fr `Date (sans heure)`.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-gvxx96`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fa2b9fc7dfa26ab486be4a9a604b5d6922da414a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts, packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts + packages/lint/src/i18n-walk.ts

Delta round on the record in comment 7195508409 (head `8f1f70ffa5`, PASS with S1 open). Read: card #36950 (body and both comments), this PR's body, file list and net diff against `main`, the earlier record, the delta `8f1f70ffa5..fa2b9fc7df` in full, and the check-runs on this head. Placeholders below are written `TYPE`, `PATH`, `VALUE`.

The delta is one commit over two prose files, 4 lines in and 4 out: `.changeset/36950-metadata-form-option-labels.md` (one sentence) and `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx` (one table cell, one sentence). No file under `packages/` moved, so the two `hits` files, the extractor, the tests and the eleven packs are byte-identical to the head the earlier record judged. `main` has not touched any of the three scoped files, the strict-object helper or that docs page since this branch's merge-base.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set, widened: right, unchanged by the delta.** A `metadataForms.TYPE.fields.PATH` entry accepts `options`, a record from string to string (`translation.zod.ts:2551`), on the three faces built from `appTranslationDataShape`. Nothing is narrowed.
- **Refusal text: right, unchanged by the delta.** `choices` and `values` on that entry are refused before and after this PR. The two `aliases` rows at `translation.zod.ts:2546` only put the rename into the unknown-key message.
- **Served surface: right, unchanged by the delta.** `resolveMetadataFormLabels` overlays `options[].label` by option value for the request locale (`i18n-resolver.ts:6258-6264`). Its server caller is still `packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts:3691`. No export or signature moves.
- **Extractor surface: right, unchanged by the delta.** `walkFormField` emits one entry per option at `PATH`, `options`, `VALUE` (`i18n-walk.ts:2795-2800`), under the same path rule and the same guard as the resolver.
- **The delta implies no accept-set or public-surface change.** It edits CHANGELOG source text and one hand-written docs page. Neither is read by a parser, a gate or a served route.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: added` are right, and both lines are in the PR body and in the changeset body. The changeset frontmatter is unchanged: `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/lint` and `@objectstack/platform-objects` patch.
- The changeset's four bullets now all match the tree. The one that did not is the sentence the delta rewrote; see S1 under ④.
- `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag, the `choices` / `values` pair mirrors the object-field face:** answered, right. `FieldTranslationSchema` carries the same two rows (`translation.zod.ts:227`), and both are rename pointers. The changeset and the PR body now say so in the same words as the schema behaves.
- **Dev flag, a non-string option value is passed through and not stringified:** answered, right on this face, as in the earlier record. `FormSelectOptionSchema` (`packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts:4030`) takes its `value` from `SelectOptionSchema`, a string. The delta does not touch it.
- **Dev flag, `check:i18n-coverage` could not be measured locally:** answered by CI. `Lint & Repo Gates` is green on this head.
- **`Skills-docs: none`:** holds for `skills/**`. The only mention on this head is `skills/objectstack-i18n/SKILL.md:180`, the group name with no leaf under it. The docs half the earlier record raised as N2 is fixed in this delta.
- **`open_questions`:** none on the card or the PR.
- **SQL push-down:** nothing to judge. The delta is prose, and the PR adds no query, no id materialisation and no join.
- **Check-runs, newest run per name, read 2026-11-26T15:37Z:** every one is `success` or `skipped`, none failed. All ten `Test Core` shards, the aggregate `Test Core`, `Build Docs`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Spec property liveness` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are green. `PR-body guards` has one `cancelled` run superseded by a later `success`. `Lint UI` reads `skipped`.
- **Landing class:** 3,879 changed lines, over 3,000, so the PR lands on an authorized APPROVED review. None is on the PR at read time. This record does not lift that.
- **Author:** `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no off-relay author note.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

S1: closed.

What closes it, read on the tree. `.changeset/36950-metadata-form-option-labels.md:12` now reads that `choices` and `values` "are refused there, as on the object-field face, and the refusal names `options` as the key to write". Each of the three claims holds:
- Refused: neither spelling is a key of the strict entry's shape, and an `aliases` row is read only on the unknown-key path (`packages/spec/src/shared/strict-object.ts`, the `aliases` option; `packages/spec/src/shared/suggestions.zod.ts:339-372`).
- As on the object-field face: `FieldTranslationSchema` at `translation.zod.ts:227` lists `values` and `choices` with the same target.
- The refusal names `options`: the message is built as a rename from the written key to `options`, the wording `translation.test.ts:1490-1496` pins on a sibling face.

The PR body's "Spec, translation slot" bullet carries the corrected wording too, and adds that an alias row is a rename hint and not an accepted spelling. No other file in the diff calls the two spellings accepted: a search of the net diff outside the generated packs finds the word only on the `aliases` row itself.

**The delta, read in full.**
- **Changeset sentence:** right, as above. It is the only line of the file that moved.
- **`i18n-standard.mdx:575`, the resolver table's first row:** now names each `options[].label` by its `value` beside label, helpText and placeholder, under `resolveMetadataFormLabels`. That is what the resolver does (`i18n-resolver.ts:6258-6264`), and it sits in the column headed "What the panel reads", which is right: the console's select draws the option's `label` and keys on its `value` (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/SchemaForm.tsx:2447-2475`).
- **`i18n-standard.mdx:586-587`:** "Only `label` crosses over to the schema (as `title`); `helpText`, `placeholder` and the option names stay on the form." I tried to break this against `resolveMetadataFormSchemaTitles` (`i18n-resolver.ts:6511-6526`): it walks every `fields` path of the bundle, reads the `label` attribute alone, and skips an entry that has none. An entry that carries only `options` therefore writes nothing to the schema, and no option name reaches a schema node. The sentence holds.
- The delta adds no new claim that the tree does not back, and it makes no finding on an unchanged hunk reachable.

**`packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts`: holds.** Unchanged since the earlier record. The schema is the thing S1 measured the prose against, and it was right then.

**`packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts`: holds.** Unchanged since the earlier record.

**`packages/lint/src/i18n-walk.ts` (implementing): agrees with the contract.** Unchanged since the earlier record.

Nits:
- N2: closed. Fixed on the prose face, in the two places the earlier record named.
- N1 (nit, comment in a reviewed file): still open as an accepted deviation. `i18n-resolver.ts:6078` and `:6088` name the FormView route as label, helpText and placeholder only, and the `resolveMetadataFormSchemaTitles` jsdoc at `:6494-6495` says the same. The docs page now says more than these comments do. A fix moves a reviewed file, so it goes with the next touch.
- N3 (nit, jsdoc in a reviewed file): still open as an accepted deviation. `translation.zod.ts:2496`, "so a choice is named the same wherever the row is rendered", is true of the served form only.

Out-of-diff notes (read, not reviewed), both carried from the earlier record and unchanged by the delta:
1. The console's curated inspectors for report, dashboard, page and view localize the bundled spec form from a console-side table that carries no `options`, so the new slot may not reach those panels. It was not run, since this review is read-only. It is a reading for the seat, and a card if it reproduces.
2. `form-option-labels.test.ts` is in the remainder, the lane seat's ACCEPT. It refuses any option name byte-equal to its English label in all ten locales and keeps no decision ledger for loanwords.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-gvxx96`
